title: Design System: Horos
legacyTokenNames: Token names are legacy from the earlier Prism cyan/amber palette: cyan = accent red, cyan-deep = deep red, amber = coral tint, amber-deep = ember, ice = blush, navy/glass = graphite, info = neutral grey.

midnight.purpose: Page ground; text on accent fills; inset wells.

navy.purpose: Legacy token name. Translucent panel body, input fill, chips.

glass.purpose: Seller segment of split bars, hover fills, skeletons, tracks.

cyan.purpose: Legacy token name. The single accent: money toward the pool, active state, focus, repaid figures.

cyan-deep.purpose: Far stop of the primary gradient on fills and split segments.

ice.purpose: Legacy token name. Mono addresses, number flash, sweep-run light.

amber.purpose: Legacy token name. Lighter second tone of the red, only where two shares must be told apart: seller's share, parked cash, risk, human judgement.

amber-deep.purpose: Legacy token name. Far stop of the tint gradient; edge terminus.

white.purpose: Primary text; secondary text via opacity 85/75/70%.

danger.purpose: Rejections, freezes, defaults, errors. Near the accent hue; always pair with an icon or label.

info.purpose: Pale grey for routine agent actions and monitor verdicts.

display.purpose: The landing's single offer line only.

headline.purpose: Landing section heads, written as sentences.

title.purpose: Loop stage names; lien headings at 18px.

label.purpose: Metric labels and metadata, sentence case.

shadows.name: glow-accent
shadows.purpose: Active nav pill and active tab pill (accent red).

shadows.name: red-edge
shadows.purpose: 1px masked border gradient (not a shadow) on the hero panel per view, search field and active pills.

motion.name: sweep-run
motion.purpose: Light crossing the pool segment when a repayment lands.

motion.name: specular
motion.purpose: Cursor-tracked button edge light; off on coarse pointers.

motion.name: console-line
motion.purpose: Exchange console lines coming into focus.

components.name: Primary Button

narrative.overview:
A dark ledger read through glass. Everything sits on near-black graphite, inside translucent graphite panels, and the only light in the room is one red: the accent marks money moving, the system acting and anything that needs attention. The system's signature is the red edge, a 1px border that runs bright red at the top-left, fades to near-nothing along the sides and returns as a deeper red at the bottom-right.

Token names in code are legacy from the earlier Prism cyan/amber palette: `--cyan` is the accent, `--cyan-deep` the deep accent, `--amber` the lighter red tint, `--amber-deep` the ember red, `--ice` the blush, `--navy` and `--glass` are graphite. Read the names as slots, not hues.

The world is dense but quiet. Numbers are the heroes: tabular, semibold, and alive (they count to their new value and flash blush when they grow). Prose is sentence-case Inter at moderate weight, set narrow (48 to 72ch). Mono is reserved for real protocol text: addresses, `payTo`, HTTP lines, flags. Motion is one curve everywhere (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) and always means something arrived, moved or settled.

Light follows the pointer. Buttons carry a specular edge whose bright arc points toward the cursor and brightens as it approaches, so the interface feels like a lit object rather than a flat page.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite ground with two faint fixed red radial washes (accent top-left, tint bottom-right).
Translucent graphite panels with a hairline border and a soft drop; the red edge on the panel that matters most per view.
One accent hue, red. Where two shares must be told apart, the lighter red tint is the second tone; never a second hue.
Tabular semibold numbers that animate between values.
Mono only for protocol and chain text.
One easing curve; motion reports state changes, not decoration.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Red is the only accent hue. The full-strength red means toward the pool or the system acting; the lighter coral tint is the second tone of the same red, for the seller's share or a human deciding. A split bar is always accent then smoke (or tint), left to right, and the edge always runs bright red top-left to ember bottom-right. Never introduce a second accent hue.

rules.name: The Opacity Ladder Rule
rules.body: Secondary text is white at reduced opacity (85 / 75 / 70%) or muted; do not introduce new grey hexes.

rules.name: The Protocol-Only Mono Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only on text a machine produced or consumes: addresses, hashes, endpoints, headers, flag codes, `payTo`. Never for labels, numbers or decoration.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the system is uppercase or letter-spaced as a label. Headings are sentences; labels are sentence-case muted text. (Uppercase appears only when quoting a real protocol header such as PAYMENT-REQUIRED.)

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every figure that can change carries tabular numerals so live updates don't jitter.

rules.name: The Red Edge Rule
rules.body: The accent-to-ember 1px edge (masked gradient border) marks the one hero panel per view (landing console and closing panel, ledger intro, explorer search, seller header), the search field, and the active pill. It is a signature, not a default border; ordinary panels use the hairline.

rules.name: The Lit From Within Rule
rules.body: Glows are inner-and-outer light in the signal's own color, never a dark offset shadow.

dos: **Do** keep red as the only accent hue; use the lighter coral tint only as a second tone where two shares must be told apart (The One Red Rule).
**Do** give exactly one panel per view the red edge; everything else uses the 1px hairline.
**Do** set every changing figure in tabular semibold and animate it with the shared count-up.
**Do** use the single ease cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) and animate with transform, opacity and filter only.
**Do** make active states a single shared pill that glides, rather than per-item highlights.
**Do** step secondary text down by white opacity (85 / 75 / 70%) or muted.
**Do** label testnet mocks and operator overrides in the UI text itself.
donts: **Don't** use JetBrains Mono for anything that isn't protocol or chain text.
**Don't** set uppercase, letter-spaced eyebrows or kickers above headings.
**Don't** use dark offset drop shadows to lift components; depth comes from glass, the edge and inner glow.
**Don't** add a second accent hue, swap the edge gradient direction, or rely on hue alone to tell the accent from danger.
**Don't** introduce sharp (0px) corners or new grey hexes outside the neutral set.
**Don't** animate width/height for progress; grow fills with scaleX.
